To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have observed the dark nebula Barnard 68 at 850 μm and 1.2mm, and we have determined the dust emissivity at 850  and 1. 2mm.

the dust emissivity is not linearly related to the extinction, that the emissivity at 850  μ m is higher than expected from the emissivity at V -band and that the emissivity is higher than expected for the grain size distribution in the interstellar medium.
we have observed Barnard 68 at 850 μm and 1.1 mm and find that the submillimetre emission correlates with the extinction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of dust in dark clouds, in particular with the study of the properties of the dust grains.
the study of the dust properties and the star formation in the dark cloud Barn 68.
the study of the dust emission in dark clouds and its relation with the extinction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a clear need for a better understanding of the physical and chemical processes that affect the dust properties in dark clouds.
the dust emissivities in the 850  μ m–1.2 cm wavelength regime are not yet well determined.
the submm/mm emissivity is not well determined and depends on the physical conditions in the cloud and the grain properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the submillimetre emissivity of the dust is higher than expected for diffuse interstellar material, but lower than expected for grains grown by coagulation and coagulation+aggregation.
dust grains in dense clouds are not much different from grains in the diffuse ISM, but they have grown somewhat larger.

the submillimetre dust emissivity in Barnard 68 is consistent with that of the diffuse dust in the Galaxy, and that the millimetre dust emissivities are consistent with the predictions of models for grain growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dust emissivity at submillimetre wavelengths is not a constant.
, while we can measure the dust emissivities in a single object, the interpretation of these results is still very uncertain.
the dust emissivity in the 850-1200  μ m range is not well determined, and that the emissivity is likely to be a strong function of environment.
